The isomorphism $i^{\circ}\bigl(\tau^{\circ}(\mathscr{F}_{1})\star_{X}\tau^{\circ}(\mathscr{F}_{2})\bigr)\cong i^{\bullet}\bigl(\tau^{\circ}(\mathscr{F}_{1})\star_{X}\tau^{\circ}(\mathscr{F}_{2})\bigr)$ observed in Lemma 7.8 can also be deduced from more general considerations related to universal local acyclicity; see [Z4, Theorem A.2.6 and proof of Proposition 5.4.2].

We now analyze the convolution diagram over $U=X^{2}\smallsetminus\Delta_{X}$:

$\textstyle{(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\times\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X})|_{U}}$ $\textstyle{\bigl(\widetilde{\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\times\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}}\bigl)\bigl|_{U}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{p}$ $\scriptstyle{q}$ $\textstyle{(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\widetilde{\times}\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X})|_{U}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{\sim}$ $\scriptstyle{m}$ $\scriptstyle{\pi\circ m}$ $\textstyle{\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X^{2}}|_{U}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{\wr}$ $\scriptstyle{\pi}$ $\textstyle{(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\times\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X})|_{U}.}$

(7.5)

Here $\pi$ is the isomorphism of (7.3), defined by

$(\mathcal{F},\nu,x_{1},x_{2})\mapsto\bigl((\mathcal{F}_{1},\nu_{1},x_{1}),(\mathcal{F}_{2},\nu_{2},x_{2})\bigr),$

where $\mathcal{F}_{i}$ is obtained by gluing the trivial bundle on $X_{R}\smallsetminus x_{i}$ and the bundle $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{D}_{x_{i},R}$ using  $\nu$. We note that there exists an isomorphism

$\bigl(\widetilde{\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\times\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}}\bigl)\bigl|_{U}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Bigl((\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\times\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X})\times_{X^{2}}(X\times G_{X,\mathcal{O}})\Bigr)\bigl|_{U}$

defined by

$(\mathcal{F}_{1},\nu_{1},\mu_{1},\mathcal{F}_{2},\nu_{2},x_{1},x_{2})\mapsto\Bigl(((\mathcal{F}_{1},\nu_{1},x_{1}),(\mathcal{F}_{2},\nu_{2},x_{2})),(x_{1},(x_{2},\mu_{1}^{-1}\circ\nu_{1}|_{\mathcal{D}_{x_{2},R}}))\Bigr).$

Under this identification, the maps $p$ and $\pi\circ m\circ q$ identify with

$\textstyle{(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\times\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X})|_{U}}$ $\textstyle{\bigl[(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\times\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X})\underset{X^{2}}{\times}(X\times G_{X,\mathcal{O}})\bigr]\bigl|_{U}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{p_{1}}$ $\scriptstyle{a}$ $\textstyle{(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\times\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X})|_{U},}$

where $p_{1}$ is the projection on the first factor and $a$ is the action of $G_{X,\mathcal{O}}$ on the second copy of $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}$.

It follows that if we identify the three spaces on the right-hand side of the convolution diagram (7.5), then for any $\mathscr{M}_{1}$, $\mathscr{M}_{2}$ in $\mathrm{Perv}_{G_{X,\mathcal{O}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X},\mathbf{k})$, the equivariant structure of $\mathscr{M}_{2}$ leads to canonical identifications

$\textstyle{(\mathscr{M}_{1}\,\widetilde{\boxtimes}\,\mathscr{M}_{2})|_{U}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\textstyle{(\mathscr{M}_{1}\star_{X}\mathscr{M}_{2})|_{U}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\textstyle{(\mathscr{M}_{1}\boxtimes\mathscr{M}_{2})|_{U}.}$

(7.6)

Consider now the open embedding $j:(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\times\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X})|_{U}\overset{<<ref:eqn:GrBD-away-diag>>}{\cong}\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X^{2}}|_{U}\hookrightarrow\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X^{2}}$.
card.label: Remark 7.9

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
